Nobody covers all fourteen layers of the enterprise estate. The gaps in your candidate's row are your integration work, and they are better discovered before the contract than after.

<GuideFigure id="vendor-coverage-matrix" fullWidth />

Start with **[the 30 vendor questions](/vendors/the-30-vendor-questions)**: the checklist that turns a demo meeting into an evidence meeting. Six of the thirty are disqualifiers where they apply.

Then read the profile for anyone on your shortlist. Each states what the research could verify, what is vendor-published, and what could not be established at all:

- [Microsoft](/library/vendors/profiles/microsoft): the strongest identity answers in the market; per-user pricing removed the brake on agent proliferation.
- [Salesforce](/library/vendors/profiles/salesforce): stated permission parity between embedded and external paths; agents do not pause before consequential actions by default.
- [ServiceNow](/library/vendors/profiles/servicenow): the most credible cross-estate governance product, which is also a strategic dependency at the layer you wanted neutral.
- [SAP](/library/vendors/profiles/sap): embedded-only by policy, an architecture constraint on your whole estate.
- [AWS](/library/vendors/profiles/aws): the strongest runtime answer, including no CPU charge while agents wait.
- [Google](/library/vendors/profiles/google): the payment protocol that proves the deterministic boundary, and its sharpest caveat, from the same vendor.
- [Anthropic](/library/vendors/profiles/anthropic): the strongest structural interoperability answer, because the standards are open rather than owned.
- [OpenAI](/library/vendors/profiles/openai): the thinnest profile relative to prominence, which is a statement about available evidence, not the product.
- [Gateways and identity](/library/vendors/profiles/gateways-and-identity): extend your API management by default; buy dedicated conditionally.
- [Evaluation and observability](/library/vendors/profiles/evals-and-observability): the category that consolidated hardest in twelve months; instrument through a translation layer.

Two facts date this section fastest: the consolidation waves in security and observability, and the telemetry conventions that are still not stable. Both sit on a re-verification list and are re-checked quarterly.
